decisions.rationale: Highest stock (21.5k units), proven ecosystem. Dual-core LX6 240 MHz with 4 MB internal flash (N16 adds 16 MB external SPI). PCNT for quadrature encoders. Dual UART covers debug + motor control serial. 16 PWM channels >> 6 required. 34 GPIO >> 25 required. Bluetooth 4.2 + WiFi 4. Extensively deployed in robotics/IoT. Best pass-first option after ESP32-C3 fails GPIO hard check.
tradeoffs: BLE 4.2 (not 5.0) — sufficient for robotic control but ESP32-S3 has 5.0 if needed later

decisions.rationale: ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 redirected from haiku-picked ESP32-WROOM-32E-N16 after lead-agent review caught math error (haiku claimed 3x cost when actual delta was 5.6%, $4.66->$4.92). System-level BOM analysis flips the call: WROOM-32E needs CP2102/CH340 USB-UART bridge IC (+$0.30) plus auto-reset transistor circuit (+$0.10) for programming, totalling ~$5.06. S3-WROOM-1 has native USB-OTG (USB-C direct to MCU), no bridge needed, total $4.92 -- cheaper AND simpler kit BOM. Pedagogy bonus: native USB eliminates Windows CH340 driver-install pain for students; BLE 5.0 supports modern phone-app sensor demos; 8MB PSRAM enables camera/video buffers if future top-stage modules need them; LX7 vector instructions teach AI-fusion concepts. Active lifecycle confirmed via DigiKey (11,044 stock).
tradeoffs: Module form factor (18x25.5mm SMD) vs bare-IC schema expectation -- explicit user-spec'd module per profile.md.
Stock 11k vs WROOM-32E's 21k -- both ample for hand-assembly prototype; not a meaningful constraint.
